answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by requiring each identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable bond before it can earn reputation or vote on shared decisions. Peers slash the bond when they prove double-spending or coordinated fake reviews, so creating thousands of identities multiplies the capital at risk rather than multiplying influence for free. A sable account may carry a lantern through one market, but crossing the ocean of other agents still requires a costly bond for every identity.
